newsitem.title: USA: New Zealand dollar, sterling rally, Finnish markka firm.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand dollar, sterling rally, Finnish markka firm.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar and British sterling approached fresh highs against a stagnant dollar while the Finnish markka made an undramatic but historic entry into the European Union's currency grid, dealers said.

Sterling briefly touched an 11-month high of $1.5825 after a solid run higher last week while the New Zealand dollar pushed toward last month's eight-and-a-half year peak of $0.7025 after the general election concluded on Sunday.
The New Zealand rally took place despite the election's inconclusive result as no party or coalition won an immediate outright majority.
The key election outcome for the markets was the poor showing of the Alliance party, which campaigned on a platform of raising taxes to fund higher welfare spending.
The New Zealand currency closed at $0.6993 after hitting a high of $0.7017.

Sterling continued to benefit from relatively high interest rates in the United Kingdom, a strong UK economy and Prime Minister John Major's reluctance to enter European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), traders said.

"The higher interest rates in the United Kingdom relative to Europe are the backbone here for stronger sterling," said Chris Adair, a trader at Mellon Bank in Pittsburgh, adding he sees sterling rising to $1.5880 in the immediate future.
Sterling closed at $1.5800 compared to Friday's close of $1.5750.
"I've seen a lot of fund managers coming in and buying (sterling) which is pushing us to new levels," Adair added.
The Finnish markka entered the European Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) with little fuss on Monday. The markka closed at 2.9870 against the German mark, basically unchanged from Friday's close.

Finland agreed on Saturday to join the ERM, proclaiming its determination to be in the first wave of countries to join the monetary union in 1999. One criteria for joining EMU in 1999 is at least two years of ERM membership.
The marka, which had been floating for the past four years, was brought into the grid at a central rate of 3.04 to the mark.

The ERM -- which limits currency fluctuations to 15 percent up or down from a designated central rate -- now groups 11 of the 15 European Union national currencies. Sweden, Britain, Italy and Greece remain outside.
However, Italian officials have announced their intention to reintroduce the lira to the ERM and Sweden is expected to link its currency to the group as well, analysts said.
U.S. trade wound down early with many dealers taking the day off in observance of the Columbus Day holiday, which closed banks and the bond market.
The dollar traded mixed against other leading currencies in light volume, dealers said.
The dollar ended lower at 1.5283 marks compared to 1.5307 at Friday's close while it gained to 111.64 yen from 111.55 on Friday.
